clips.send: Earth's rotation. One spin every 24 hours, west to east. Earth spins once on its axis about every 24 hours, from west to east. Seen from above the North Pole, it turns counterclockwise. That is why the Sun seems to rise in the east and set in the west. At the equator the ground moves about 1,670 km/h (1,040 mph)!
